problems: The 'Pale Ochre Twig' marker is a clean, cream-white lashed arch. In the cell and the vignette it looks like a bleached bone or a plastic hoop, not sticks and mud (Sami's note 2). It is also the brightest object on the free lot, so it reads as manufactured.
elements.fix: Recolour the twigs to dark bark browns (#5a3a22 to #7a5232). Make it 2-3 crooked, unequal sticks with slight random tilts, pushed into a wide, lumpy dark mud mound (#6b4a2e) with a few pebbles. For the claim cue, tie one small ochre or red hide rag to the top. Keep the overall height around 1.1 m so it still reads at stream scale.

problems: The 'Heavy-Sided Wild Pine' is three stacked, symmetric cones on a straight trunk, a tidy Christmas-tree silhouette. That breaks Sami's note 6 (wild, irregular, uneven trees).
The 'Torn Birch' is a perfectly straight pale pole with three sphere blobs. It reads as a sapling or a sculpture, not torn woodland.
elements.fix: Pine: tilt the trunk 8-15 degrees and offset the foliage tiers off-axis. Give the tiers unequal sizes, put one broken, bare branch stub on one side, and leave one side sparse. Birch: bend the trunk (two segments at different angles), add a snapped top or a dead fork, and use 4-5 foliage clumps of different sizes clustered on one side. Match the irregularity of the 'Wild trees' column, which already works.

problems: The sledge ruts are straight, evenly spaced dark bars in parallel pairs. They read like laid planks or rail sleepers on the mud track, which is an engineered look in the Stone Age.
elements.fix: Swap the bars for wavering, uneven rut troughs: several short segments at slightly different angles, widths and lengths, darker and wetter (#4a2f1c). Add puddle blobs and hoofprint or footprint dents. Avoid any straight run longer than about 2 m.
